programme: STAT1 and IRF9 carry an interferon-responsive signaling axis that feeds CIITA, whose own target set (HLA-DMA/DMB, HLA-DOA/DOB, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DRA, HLA-B/C/E/F, plus feedback onto IRF1, IRF2 and STAT1 itself) is essentially the MHC class II antigen-presentation machinery. Together these three factors describe glial/immune cells sensing interferon and switching on MHC-II-mediated antigen presentation in brain tissue.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this axis marks reactive, interferon-activated microglia and astrocytes: STAT1 is induced in microglia and linked to cognitive deficit and IL-1β output (41676156, 41206011, 40968664), and CIITA sits among the NLR-family changes reported in AD mouse brain and patients (40066444) — consistent with MHC-II upregulation on disease-associated microglia rather than with lymphocyte-driven autoimmunity.
role_in_b: In multiple sclerosis the same axis is closer to the disease's known engine: IFN-beta, a mainstay MS therapy, works by sustaining STAT1-dependent interferon responses (42267917), and CIITA-driven MHC class II presentation is the molecular basis for autoantigen presentation to CD4+ T cells, with CIITA's involvement in the EAE/vitamin-D model captured directly (33304315). IRF9 evidence here is about type-I interferon pathway integrity (39958336, 41474826) rather than a novel finding.
shared_axis: Both diseases run interferon-driven glial/immune activation in brain tissue that culminates in CIITA-mediated MHC class II induction — in MS this presents myelin-derived antigen to infiltrating T cells, while in AD the same STAT1/CIITA machinery is repurposed by reactive microglia/astrocytes responding to protein-aggregate or damage signals, giving two different diseases a common downstream antigen-presentation module even though the trigger differs.
reasoning: STAT1 and CIITA are each independently placed in both diseases by retrieved papers, including two papers explicitly discussing both diseases together (37480622, 36078052) and one that names both in its abstract (33304315), which is why this clears 'unexpected' — the connection isn't undocumented. But IRF9 has no retrieved AD evidence at all, and the causal ordering (STAT1→CIITA→MHC-II) is supplied from general pathway knowledge rather than stated together in any one retrieved paper, so this stays 'moderate' rather than 'strong'.
support: 40968664 (STAT1 induction attenuated by creatine in AD model); 41676156 (microglial STAT1 upregulation drives cognitive deficit in AD); 41206011 (Tyro3-STAT1 axis controls IL-1β in AD models); 42267917 (IFN-beta therapy sustains STAT1-dependent IFN responses in MS); 37480622 (joint AD/MS paper: S1P receptor antagonist reduces TLR4 neuroinflammation and Aβ clearance); 36078052 (joint paper: cytokine-stimulated astrocyte transcriptomes relevant to both diseases); 40066444 (CIITA/NLR-family changes in AD mouse model and patients); 33304315 (CIITA/vitamin D haplotype effect on EAE, explicitly discusses both diseases); 39958336 (IRF9 as diagnostic gene in MS); 41474826 (IRF9/type-I interferon pathway targeted by viral antagonists, MS-relevant context).
how_to_falsify: In a CIITA-conditional-knockout microglia/astrocyte line, compare MHC-II induction and STAT1/IRF9 target-gene response to IFN-gamma stimulation between an AD model (e.g., 5xFAD-derived glia) and an EAE/MS model; if CIITA loss abolishes MHC-II induction and the associated inflammatory phenotype in one disease model but not the other, the shared-axis claim is wrong. A simpler check: block IFNGR/JAK-STAT1 signaling upstream in both models and see whether CIITA and its HLA targets fail to rise in both.
caveats: Both diseases are sampled from brain tissue only, and the 208 patient-group comparisons come from just 9 independent cohort pairs, so the recurrence counts reflect correlated subgroups more than fully independent replications. The tissue-generic exclusion list correctly removed microglial/myeloid master regulators (MEF2C, CEBPB, MITF, HDAC1) that would otherwise have been mistaken for the 'obvious' shared mechanism — CIITA/STAT1/IRF9 survived independently of those. IRF9's role rests entirely on MS-side papers (silence for AD is not evidence of absence, per the read rules). Other recurrent factors here (E2F2, ID1, NR2F6, GTF2I, FOXQ1, YBX1, THAP1, SMARCA1, ZNF91) track separable programmes — cell-cycle re-entry, Th17 T-cell restraint, cell differentiation — and were left out of this account because the record does not connect them mechanistically to the STAT1/IRF9/CIITA axis.
